title: Histotechnologist IHC lab (FT Nights Tuesday - Saturday)

cond_0001.intro: Processes patient surgical pathology specimens to paraffin, embeds tissue in paraffin, performs paraffin blocks using microtomes, stains prepared tissue, coverslips slides and assesses stains and sections microscopically for quality with a focus on immunohistochemistry testing. Prepares and performs various staining techniques on all immunohistochemistry testing in Histology: Including processing patient surgical pathology specimens to paraffin, embed tissue in paraffin, paraffin blocks using microtomes, stain prepared tissue, coverslip slides, and assess stains and sections microscopically for quality. Validates and optimizes new or replaced antibodies according to lab policy and assures quality control of all cases stained. May be required to be liaison in absence of Supervisor and lead the team. Will be expected to communicate directly with Supervisor on issues requiring any policy change or result delays or quality of result concerns.
cond_0001.responsibilities: All immunohistochemical staining is stained daily using approved automated stainers and in accordance with lab policy control material is stained at the same time the case is to assure quality staining. Validation and optimization of new antibodies and procedures are run according to approved lab policy and CAP guidelines daily. Ensures recycling is collected daily as part of the Medical Center's QI initiatives and all employees must be part of the program. Maintain continuing education to meet their registration requirements and developments in histology and participate in mandatory and voluntary continuing education, competency testing, and Quality Assurance. Handles all antibodies and their necessary kits and controls and the equipment to perform these tests. Controls must be maintained and recorded along with other quality measures in accordance with department and CAP guidelines. Maintain and validate adequacy for controls for all antibodies used in the lab to produce staining according to CAP guidelines and hospital protocol. Prepare cases for pathologists' review, and maintain extensive files of blocks and slides to assure accuracy and assure quality control is in place according to policy and lab guidelines.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree from a NAACLS-accredited histology technician/technology program, or a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited college or university with valid HT credentials and 3 years applicable experience, or 5 years experience including special stains and immunohistochemistry.
Advanced skills with Microsoft applications which may include Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or Access and other web-based applications. May produce complex documents, perform analysis and maintain databases.
Preferred Requirements
AS/BS degree.
Registration ASCP Registered.

cond_0269.intro: We are looking for a Histotechnologist to join our team. In this role, you will own the full workflow of immunohistochemistry testing in Histology — from processing patient surgical pathology specimens to paraffin, embedding tissue, cutting paraffin blocks using microtomes, staining prepared tissue, coverslipping slides, and assessing stains and sections microscopically for quality. You will validate and optimize new or replaced antibodies according to lab policy and ensure quality control across all stained cases. In the absence of the Supervisor, you may be called on to lead the team and serve as liaison. You will communicate directly with the Supervisor on issues involving policy changes, result delays, or quality concerns.
cond_0269.responsibilities:
Execute all immunohistochemical staining daily using approved automated stainers and in accordance with lab policy; ensure control material is stained alongside each case to confirm staining quality.
Drive validation and optimization of new antibodies and procedures according to approved lab policy and CAP guidelines on a daily basis.
Ensure recycling is collected daily as part of the Medical Center's QI initiatives; all employees must participate in the program.
Maintain continuing education to meet registration requirements and stay current with developments in histology; take part in mandatory and voluntary continuing education, competency testing, and Quality Assurance.
Manage all antibodies, their necessary kits and controls, and the equipment required to perform these tests.
Maintain and record controls along with other quality measures in accordance with department and CAP guidelines.
Validate and maintain adequacy of controls for all antibodies used in the lab to produce staining according to CAP guidelines and hospital protocol.
Prepare cases for pathologists' review and maintain extensive files of blocks and slides to ensure accuracy and quality control in accordance with policy and lab guidelines.
cond_0269.requirements:
Bachelor's degree from a NAACLS-accredited histology technician/technology program, or a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited college or university with valid HT credentials and 3 years applicable experience, or 5 years experience including special stains and Immunohistochemistry. AS/BS degree preferred.
Advanced skills with Microsoft applications which may include Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or Access and other web-based applications. May produce complex documents, perform analysis and maintain databases.
Registration ASCP Registered preferred.
Decision Making: Ability to make decisions that are guided by general instructions and practices requiring some interpretation. May make recommendations for solving problems of moderate complexity and importance.

Independence of Action: Ability to follow precedents and procedures. May set priorities and organize work within general guidelines. Seeks assistance when confronted with difficult and/or unpredictable situations. Work progress is monitored by the supervisor/manager.
Written Communications: Ability to summarize and communicate in English moderately complex information in varied written formats to internal and external customers.
Oral Communications: Ability to comprehend and converse in English to communicate effectively with medical center staff, patients, families, and external customers.
Knowledge: Ability to demonstrate a full working knowledge of standard concepts, practices, procedures, and policies with the ability to use them in varied situations.
Team Work: Ability to lead collaborative teams for larger projects or groups both internal and external to the Medical Center and across functional areas. Results have implications for the management and operations of multiple areas of the organization.
Customer Service: Ability to provide a high level of customer service to patients, visitors, staff, and external customers in a professional, service-oriented, respectful manner using skills in active listening and problem-solving. Ability to remain calm in stressful situations.
Physical Nature of the Job: Sedentary work: Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally in carrying, lifting, pushing, and pulling objects. Sitting most of the time, with walking and standing required only occasionally.

cond_0349.intro: This role processes patient surgical pathology specimens with a focus on immunohistochemistry testing. Core work includes embedding tissue in paraffin, sectioning blocks using microtomes, staining prepared tissue, coverslipping slides, and assessing stains and sections microscopically for quality. The position also validates and optimizes new or replaced antibodies per lab policy and maintains quality control across all stained cases. In the absence of the Supervisor, the role may serve as liaison and lead the team. The role is expected to report directly to the Supervisor on issues involving policy changes, result delays, or quality concerns.
cond_0349.responsibilities:
All immunohistochemical staining is completed using approved automated stainers in accordance with lab policy; control material is stained alongside each case to confirm staining quality.
Validation and optimization of new antibodies and procedures are conducted according to approved lab policy and CAP guidelines.
Ensures recycling is collected as part of the Medical Center's QI initiatives; all employees are required to participate in the program.
Maintains continuing education to meet registration requirements and keeps current with developments in histology; participates in mandatory and voluntary continuing education, competency testing, and Quality Assurance.
Handles all antibodies, associated kits and controls, and the equipment required to perform these tests.
Controls are maintained and recorded along with other quality measures in accordance with department and CAP guidelines.
Maintains and validates adequacy of controls for all antibodies used in the lab to produce staining according to CAP guidelines and hospital protocol.
Prepares cases for pathologists' review and maintains extensive files of blocks and slides to confirm accuracy and quality control in accordance with policy and lab guidelines.
cond_0349.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree from a NAACLS-accredited histology technician/technology program, or a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited college or university with valid HT credentials and 3 years of applicable experience, or 5 years of experience including special stains and immunohistochemistry
Working knowledge of standard concepts, practices, procedures, and policies in histology with the ability to apply them across varied situations
Ability to follow precedents and procedures, set priorities, and organize work within general guidelines; seeks assistance when confronted with difficult or unpredictable situations
Ability to summarize and communicate moderately complex information in written formats in English
Ability to comprehend and converse in English to communicate effectively with medical center staff, patients, families, and external customers
Ability to provide a high level of customer service in a professional, respectful manner using active listening and problem-solving; ability to remain calm in stressful situations
Ability to make decisions guided by general instructions and practices requiring some interpretation; may make recommendations for problems of moderate complexity
Ability to address varied problems requiring analysis or interpretation using direct observation, knowledge, and skills based on general precedents
Preferred Requirements
AS/BS degree
ASCP Registration
Advanced skills with Microsoft applications including Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or Access, and other web-based applications; ability to produce complex documents, perform analysis, and maintain databases
Ability to lead collaborative teams for larger projects or groups both internal and external to the Medical Center and across functional areas

cond_0383.intro: Processes patient surgical pathology specimens to paraffin, embeds tissue in paraffin, performs paraffin blocks using microtomes, stains prepared tissue, coverslips slides and assesses stains and sections microscopically for quality with a focus on immunohistochemistry testing. Prepares and performs various staining techniques on all immunohistochemistry testing in Histology: Including processing patient surgical pathology specimens to paraffin, embed tissue in paraffin, paraffin blocks using microtomes, stain prepared tissue, coverslip slides, and assess stains and sections microscopically for quality. Validates and optimizes new or replaced antibodies according to lab policy and assures quality control of all cases stained. May be required to be liaison in absence of Supervisor and lead the team. Will be expected to communicate directly with Supervisor on issues requiring any policy change or result delays or quality of result concerns. People tend to become stronger in this kind of histology and IHC work over time as they build experience and learn from day-to-day casework.
cond_0383.responsibilities: All immunohistochemical staining is stained daily using approved automated stainers and in accordance with lab policy control material is stained at the same time the case is to assure quality staining. Validation and optimization of new antibodies and procedures are run according to approved lab policy and CAP guidelines daily. Ensures recycling is collected daily as part of the Medical Center's QI initiatives and all employees must be part of the program. Maintain continuing education to meet their registration requirements and developments in histology and participate in mandatory and voluntary continuing education, competency testing, and Quality Assurance. Handles all antibodies and their necessary kits and controls and the equipment to perform these tests. Controls must be maintained and recorded along with other quality measures in accordance with department and CAP guidelines. Maintain and validate adequacy for controls for all antibodies used in the lab to produce staining according to CAP guidelines and hospital protocol. Prepare cases for pathologists' review, and maintain extensive files of blocks and slides to assure accuracy and assure quality control is in place according to policy and lab guidelines.
cond_0383.requirements:
Minimum Requirements:
Bachelor's degree from a NAACLS-accredited histology technician/technology program, or a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited college or university with valid HT credentials and 3 years applicable experience, or 5 years experience including special stains and Immunohistochemistry.
Advanced skills with Microsoft applications which may include Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or Access and other web-based applications. May produce complex documents, perform analysis and maintain databases.
Preferred Requirements:
AS/BS degree.
Registration ASCP Registered.

Core work includes embedding tissue in paraffin, sectioning blocks using microtomes, staining prepared tissue, coverslipping slides, and assessing stains and sections microscopically for quality. The position also validates and optimizes new or replaced antibodies per lab policy and maintains quality control across all stained cases. In the absence of the Supervisor, the role may serve as liaison and lead the team. The role is expected to report directly to the Supervisor on issues involving policy changes, result delays, or quality concerns.
cond_0421.responsibilities:
All immunohistochemical staining is completed using approved automated stainers in accordance with lab policy; control material is stained alongside each case to confirm staining quality.
Validation and optimization of new antibodies and procedures are conducted according to approved lab policy and CAP guidelines.
Ensures recycling is collected as part of the Medical Center's QI initiatives; all employees are required to participate in the program.
Maintains continuing education to meet registration requirements and keeps current with developments in histology; participates in mandatory and voluntary continuing education, competency testing, and Quality Assurance.
Handles all antibodies, associated kits and controls, and the equipment required to perform these tests.
Controls are maintained and recorded along with other quality measures in accordance with department and CAP guidelines.
Maintains and validates adequacy of controls for all antibodies used in the lab to produce staining according to CAP guidelines and hospital protocol.
Prepares cases for pathologists' review and maintains extensive files of blocks and slides to confirm accuracy and quality control in accordance with policy and lab guidelines.
cond_0421.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree from a NAACLS-accredited histology technician/technology program, or a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited college or university with valid HT credentials and 3 years of applicable experience, or 5 years of experience including special stains and immunohistochemistry
Working knowledge of standard concepts, practices, procedures, and policies in histology with the ability to apply them across varied situations
Ability to follow precedents and procedures, set priorities, and organize work within general guidelines; seeks assistance when confronted with difficult or unpredictable situations
Ability to summarize and communicate moderately complex information in written formats in English
Ability to comprehend and converse in English to communicate effectively with medical center staff, patients, families, and external customers
Ability to provide a high level of customer service in a professional, respectful manner using active listening and problem-solving; ability to remain calm in stressful situations
Ability to make decisions guided by general instructions and practices requiring some interpretation; may make recommendations for problems of moderate complexity
Ability to address varied problems requiring analysis or interpretation using direct observation, knowledge, and skills based on general precedents
Preferred Requirements
AS/BS degree
ASCP Registration
Advanced skills with Microsoft applications including Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or Access, and other web-based applications; ability to produce complex documents, perform analysis, and maintain databases
Ability to lead collaborative teams for larger projects or groups both internal and external to the Medical Center and across functional areas

You will lead validation and optimization of antibodies, ensure quality control across all cases, and take direct accountability for communicating issues, policy concerns, or result delays to the Supervisor.
cond_0440.responsibilities:
Essential Responsibilities:
Execute all immunohistochemical staining daily using approved automated stainers, ensuring control material is stained concurrently with each case in accordance with lab policy.
Drive validation and optimization of new antibodies and procedures according to approved lab policy and CAP guidelines.
Own quality control of all stained cases, maintaining and recording controls and other quality measures in line with department and CAP guidelines.
Ensure recycling is collected daily as part of the Medical Center's QI initiatives.
Maintain continuing education to meet registration requirements, and take ownership of participation in mandatory and voluntary continuing education, competency testing, and Quality Assurance.
Manage all antibodies, necessary kits, controls, and equipment required to perform IHC tests.
Validate and maintain adequacy of controls for all antibodies used in the lab to produce staining per CAP guidelines and hospital protocol.
Prepare cases for pathologists' review and maintain extensive files of blocks and slides to ensure accuracy and quality control in accordance with policy and lab guidelines.
Act as team lead in the absence of the Supervisor, directing the team and communicating directly with the Supervisor on issues requiring policy changes, result delays, or quality concerns.
cond_0440.requirements:
Minimum Requirements:
Bachelor's degree from a NAACLS-accredited histology technician/technology program, OR a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited college or university with valid HT credentials and 3 years of applicable experience, OR 5 years of experience including special stains and immunohistochemistry
Ability to make decisions guided by general instructions and practices requiring some interpretation
Ability to address varied problems requiring analysis or interpretation using direct observation, knowledge, and skills based on general precedents
Ability to follow precedents and procedures, set priorities, and organize work within general guidelines; seeks assistance when confronted with difficult or unpredictable situations
Ability to summarize and communicate moderately complex information in English in varied written formats to internal and external customers
Ability to comprehend and converse in English to communicate effectively with medical center staff, patients, families, and external customers
Full working knowledge of standard concepts, practices, procedures, and policies with the ability to apply them in varied situations
Ability to lead collaborative teams for larger projects or groups both internal and external to the Medical Center and across functional areas
Ability to provide a high level of customer service in a professional, service-oriented, respectful manner using active listening and problem-solving skills; ability to remain calm in stressful situations
Preferred Requirements:
AS/BS degree
ASCP Registration
Advanced skills with Microsoft applications including Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or Access, and other web-based applications; ability to produce complex documents, perform analysis, and maintain databases
[Company name masked] requires that all staff be vaccinated against influenza (flu) and COVID-19 as a condition of employment.

Essential Responsibilities:
All immunohistochemical staining is completed using approved automated stainers in accordance with lab policy; control material is stained alongside each case to confirm staining quality. Validation and optimization of new antibodies and procedures are run according to approved lab policy and CAP guidelines. Ensures recycling is collected as part of the Medical Center's QI initiatives. Maintains continuing education to meet registration requirements and keeps current with developments in histology; participates in mandatory and voluntary continuing education, competency testing, and Quality Assurance. Handles all antibodies, necessary kits, controls, and equipment required to perform these tests. Controls are maintained and recorded along with other quality measures in accordance with department and CAP guidelines. Validates and maintains adequacy of controls for all antibodies used in the lab to produce staining according to CAP guidelines and hospital protocol. Prepares cases for pathologists' review and maintains files of blocks and slides to confirm accuracy and quality control in accordance with policy and lab guidelines. May serve as liaison in the absence of the Supervisor and provide direction to the team as needed. Reports issues involving policy changes, result delays, or quality concerns directly to the Supervisor.
cond_0448.requirements:
Bachelor's degree from a NAACLS-accredited histology technician/technology program, or a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited college or university with valid HT credentials and 3 years applicable experience, or 5 years experience including special stains and immunohistochemistry; AS/BS degree preferred. Advanced skills with Microsoft applications including Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or Access and other web-based applications. Able to produce complex documents, perform analysis, and maintain databases. ASCP registration preferred.
Decision Making: Ability to make decisions guided by general instructions and practices requiring some interpretation. May make recommendations for solving problems of moderate complexity and importance.
Problem Solving: Ability to address varied problems requiring analysis or interpretation of the situation using direct observation, knowledge, and skills based on general precedents.
Independence of Action: Ability to follow precedents and procedures. May set priorities and organize work within general guidelines. Seeks assistance when confronted with difficult and/or unpredictable situations. Work progress is monitored by the supervisor/manager.
Written Communications: Ability to summarize and communicate in English moderately complex information in varied written formats to internal and external customers.
Oral Communications: Ability to comprehend and converse in English to communicate effectively with medical center staff, patients, families, and external customers.
Knowledge: Ability to demonstrate a full working knowledge of standard concepts, practices, procedures, and policies with the ability to use them in varied situations.
Team Work: Ability to contribute to collaborative efforts for larger projects or groups both internal and external to the Medical Center and across functional areas. Results have implications for the management and operations of multiple areas of the organization.
Customer Service: Ability to provide a high level of customer service to patients, visitors, staff, and external customers in a professional, service-oriented, respectful manner using skills in active listening and problem-solving. Ability to remain calm in stressful situations.
Physical Nature of the Job:
Sedentary work: Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally in carrying, lifting, pushing, and pulling objects. Sitting most of the time, with walking and standing required only occasionally.

This role focuses on immunohistochemistry testing and involves regular communication with supervisors, pathologists, and lab staff to maintain quality and keep cases moving. You will be expected to stay in close contact with your team and speak up directly when issues arise around policy, result delays, or quality concerns.
cond_0474.responsibilities:
All immunohistochemical staining is performed daily using approved automated stainers and in accordance with lab policy; control material is stained at the same time as the case to assure quality staining.
Validation and optimization of new antibodies and procedures are run according to approved lab policy and CAP guidelines daily.
Ensures recycling is collected daily as part of the Medical Center's QI initiatives; all employees must be part of the program.
Maintain continuing education to meet registration requirements and developments in histology, and actively participate in mandatory and voluntary continuing education, competency testing, and Quality Assurance.
Handle all antibodies and their necessary kits, controls, and equipment to perform these tests; maintain and record controls along with other quality measures in accordance with department and CAP guidelines.
Maintain and validate adequacy of controls for all antibodies used in the lab to produce staining according to CAP guidelines and hospital protocol.
Prepare cases for pathologists' review and stay in regular contact with pathologists and lab staff to assure accuracy; maintain extensive files of blocks and slides to assure quality control is in place according to policy and lab guidelines.
Communicate directly and promptly with the Supervisor on any issues requiring policy changes, result delays, or quality concerns.
May be required to act as liaison in the absence of the Supervisor and lead the team, initiating discussions to keep work on track.
cond_0474.requirements:
Minimum Requirements:
Bachelor's degree from a NAACLS-accredited histology technician/technology program, or a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited college or university with valid HT credentials and 3 years of applicable experience, or 5 years of experience including special stains and immunohistochemistry
Working knowledge of Microsoft applications, which may include Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or Access, and other web-based applications; ability to produce complex documents, perform analysis, and maintain databases
Preferred Requirements:
AS/BS degree
ASCP Registration

cond_0475.intro: This role processes patient surgical pathology specimens with a focus on immunohistochemistry testing. Core work includes embedding tissue in paraffin, sectioning blocks using microtomes, staining prepared tissue, coverslipping slides, and assessing stains and sections microscopically for quality. The position also validates and optimizes new or replaced antibodies per lab policy and maintains quality control across all stained cases. In the absence of the Supervisor, the role may serve as liaison and lead the team. The role is expected to report directly to the Supervisor on issues involving policy changes, result delays, or quality concerns.

All immunohistochemical staining is completed using approved automated stainers in accordance with lab policy; control material is stained alongside each case to confirm staining quality.
Validation and optimization of new antibodies and procedures are conducted according to approved lab policy and CAP guidelines.
Ensures recycling is collected as part of the Medical Center's QI initiatives; all employees are required to participate in the program.
Maintains continuing education to meet registration requirements and keeps current with developments in histology; participates in mandatory and voluntary continuing education, competency testing, and Quality Assurance.
Handles all antibodies, associated kits and controls, and the equipment required to perform these tests.
Controls are maintained and recorded along with other quality measures in accordance with department and CAP guidelines.
Maintains and validates adequacy of controls for all antibodies used in the lab to produce staining according to CAP guidelines and hospital protocol.
Prepares cases for pathologists' review and maintains extensive files of blocks and slides to confirm accuracy and quality control in accordance with policy and lab guidelines.

Validates and optimizes new or replaced antibodies according to lab policy and assures quality control of all cases stained. May be required to be liaison in absence of Supervisor and lead the team. Will be expected to communicate directly with Supervisor on issues requiring any policy change or result delays or quality of result concerns. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of immunohistochemistry workflows and quality control requirements.
cond_0508.responsibilities: All immunohistochemical staining is stained daily using approved automated stainers and in accordance with lab policy control material is stained at the same time the case is to assure quality staining. Validation and optimization of new antibodies and procedures are run according to approved lab policy and CAP guidelines daily. Ensures recycling is collected daily as part of the Medical Center's QI initiatives and all employees must be part of the program. Maintain continuing education to meet their registration requirements and developments in histology and participate in mandatory and voluntary continuing education, competency testing, and Quality Assurance. cond_0584.intro: We are looking for a Histotechnologist to join our team. In this role, you will own the full workflow of immunohistochemistry testing in Histology — from processing surgical pathology specimens through paraffin embedding, microtomy, staining, and microscopic quality assessment. You will lead validation and optimization of antibodies, ensure quality control across all cases, and take direct accountability for communicating issues, policy concerns, or result delays to the Supervisor.
cond_0584.responsibilities:
Essential Responsibilities:
Execute all immunohistochemical staining daily using approved automated stainers, ensuring control material is stained concurrently with each case in accordance with lab policy.
Drive validation and optimization of new antibodies and procedures according to approved lab policy and CAP guidelines.
Own quality control of all stained cases, maintaining and recording controls and other quality measures in line with department and CAP guidelines.
Ensure recycling is collected daily as part of the Medical Center's QI initiatives.
Maintain continuing education to meet registration requirements, and take ownership of participation in mandatory and voluntary continuing education, competency testing, and Quality Assurance.
Manage all antibodies, necessary kits, controls, and equipment required to perform IHC tests.
Validate and maintain adequacy of controls for all antibodies used in the lab to produce staining per CAP guidelines and hospital protocol.
Prepare cases for pathologists' review and maintain extensive files of blocks and slides to ensure accuracy and quality control in accordance with policy and lab guidelines.
Act as team lead in the absence of the Supervisor, directing the team and communicating directly with the Supervisor on issues requiring policy changes, result delays, or quality concerns.
